items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to establishing the lymphology study and requiring the department of health to study the effects of certain training criteria established by the Lymphology Association of North America
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:A10132

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the public health law, in relation to
establishing the lymphology study and requiring the department of health
to study the effects of certain training criteria established by the
Lymphology Association of North America

PURPOSE OF BILL:  This bill requires that the lymphology study examine
the effects of requiring all therapists in this state treating patients
inflicted with lymphedema to meet the training criteria established by
the Lymphology Association of North America, and specifically examine
whether such criteria would improve treatments, patient outcomes and/or
lower overall medical costs.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:  Section 1 of this bill amends the public health
law by adding a new article setting forth the lymphology study.

Section 2 of this bill establishes that the department of health with
the responsibility of administering the provisions of this article and
otherwise coordinating the state's policies with respect to the results
of the study.

Section 3 sets forth the effective date, as well as when the results are
submitted to the governor and legislature.

JUSTIFICATION:  Lymphedema is a chronic, progressive disease caused by
any reduction in the capacity of the lymphatic system to transport lymph
and drain the fluid out of the interstitial space back into the circula-
tory system. The term "edema" refers to the accumulation of an excessive
amount of fluid in tissue or organs resulting in swelling. The two major
types of lymphedema (a rare inherited condition) and secondary lymphede-
ma which is caused by a blockage or interruption of the normal fluid
through the lymphatic system.

Currently there is no general consensus among doctors regarding a
uniform standard of care for the treatment of lymphedeme which is why
this bill is so important. Physicians and medical staff who practice in
fields where this disease is uncommon may fail to correctly diagnose the
condition due to the apparent lack of information regarding this
disease. Mandatory training by the Lymphology Association of North Amer-
ica will have an immediate impact on those inflicted with the disease.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:  No history.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:; This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Establishes the Lymphology study, requiring the department of health to study the effects of certain training criteria established by the Lymphology Association of North America.
